claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct enforced entirely within Pulumi and is never sent to the cloud provider.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute, a cloud-provider deletion-protection attribute enforced by the cloud provider independently of Pulumi.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute, a cloud-provider deletion-protection attribute enforced by the cloud provider independently of Pulumi.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (`protect` not set) and still refuse to delete due to provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while the provider-side deletion protection is off.

The docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi.
GCP Cloud SQL instances (`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance`) have a `deletionProtection` attribute.
AWS RDS instances (`aws.rds.Instance`) have a `deletionProtection` attribute.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and provider/cloud-level deletion-protection attributes are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The destroy-failures troubleshooting page has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to distinguish Pulumi `protect` from resource-level deletion protection and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When destroy is blocked by the `protect` resource option, the error names a URN and mentions `protect`.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, e.g. `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster`; the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` property.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks are enforced by the cloud API, which rejects the delete call independent of Pulumi.
Azure management-lock delete errors often come back from the cloud API with an error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says.

To remove provider-enforced or cloud-enforced deletion protection, set the attribute to `false` in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches the live resource and state, then run `pulumi destroy`; setting it to false in the program alone is not enough.
If deletion protection was already disabled outside Pulumi, `pulumi refresh` synchronizes stack state with reality, and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` `deletionProtection` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` `forceDestroy` defaults to `false`, and a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` `deletionProtectionEnabled` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.

`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist; a `CanNotDelete` lock enforced by Azure Resource Manager must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of the Pulumi program.

Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered, and purge protection prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
